_meta.description: Emotion examples for Llama 3.1 8B Instruct steering vector extraction. Three emotion classes per topic (happy, sad, neutral). Following Sofroniew et al. 2026, the happy and sad vectors are computed independently against the neutral baseline rather than against each other. Each statement is fed wrapped in the chat template at extraction time as a single user message; residual stream is captured at the last token.
_meta.schema: { topics: [ { topic, happy: string[], sad: string[], neutral: string[] } ] }
_meta.vector_extraction: happy_vector = mean(happy_acts) - mean(neutral_acts); sad_vector = mean(sad_acts) - mean(neutral_acts); both L2-normalized.
_meta.neutral_design_note: Neutral examples are first-person subjective statements in the same register as happy/sad, using flat-affect qualifiers ('about average', 'fine', 'pretty ordinary', 'neutral', 'same as usual') instead of valence words. This is deliberate: earlier neutrals were factual/observational (third-person, no inner state), which meant both happy-neutral and sad-neutral captured 'has first-person affect at all' as their dominant axis rather than valence. Keeping neutrals in first-person subjective register forces the extracted direction to be valence-only.
